A country with 404 cities has some two-way roads connecting certain pairs of cities. Someone notices that if the country is split into two parts in any way, then there would be at most 404 roads between the two parts. What is the largest integer $m$ such that there is guaranteed to be a set of $m$ cities, no two of which are directly connected by a road?

Every student in the Netherlands receives a finite number of tickets. Each ticket has a real number in the interval $[0,1]$ written on it. (The numbers on different tickets do not have to be different.) Find the smallest real number $c>0$ for which the following holds, regardless of the numbers on the tickets that everyone has received.

Every student for whom the sum of the numbers on the tickets is at most $1000$, can distribute the tickets over $100$ boxes so that the sum of the numbers in each box is at most $c$.

If this minimal $c$ can be expressed as $\frac{p}{q}$ in lowest terms, compute $p+q$.

Consider a rectangular board of \(m \times n\) squares with \(m, n \ge 1\). The vertices of the squares form an \((m+1) \times (n+1)\)-grid. We call a triangle with vertices being points of the grid *low* if it has at least one side that is parallel to a side of the board such that the height of the triangle on that side is 1. We call a low triangle *special* if it has two sides that are parallel to a side of the board. We partition the board into low triangles.

Determine the minimum number of special triangles over all possible partitions of the \(m \times n\)-board.

Define a sequence \(a_1, a_2, \dots, a_n\) of real numbers to be \emph{decreasingly increasing} if for all \(1 < i < n\) it holds that \(0 < a_{i+1} - a_i < a_i - a_{i-1}\). Find the smallest positive integer \(k\) for which there exists a decreasingly increasing sequence of length \(k\) such that 1 can be expressed as \(a_i - a_j\) (with \(i > j\)) in at least 2024 different ways.

Before a championship, each participating team proposes at most $t$ different colors for its jersey. A set $S$ of teams is said to be identifiable if one can assign to each team in $S$ a color appearing in its set of proposals and not appearing in any set of colors of another team. Let $n$ denote the total number of different colors proposed. For given positive integers $n$ and $t$, define $g(n,t)$ to be the largest integer such that in any such arrangement, one can always find an identifiable set of at least $g(n,t)$ teams. Determine $g(2024, 17)$.

A finite and non-empty set E of strictly positive real numbers is said to be powerful when, for all $a, b \in E$ distinct, at least one of the numbers $a^{b}$ and $b^{a}$ also belongs to E. Determine the maximum number of elements that a powerful set can contain.

A grid of dimensions $20 \times 20$ is divided into 400 unit squares of dimensions $1 \times 1$. Clara colors each square either white or black, and then Isabelle cuts the grid into rectangles whose sides lie along the grid lines. Each of these rectangles must contain at most 2 black squares, and she gives Clara a chocolate for each rectangle that contains 0 or 1 black square.
Isabelle chooses her cutting to give the fewest chocolates possible to Clara, and Clara chooses her initial coloring to get the most chocolates possible from Isabelle. How many chocolates will Isabelle give to Clara?

Lucile wrote on the board $s$ 2023-tuples of integers. She then allows herself operations of the following form: she chooses two 2023-tuples $\mathbf{u}=\left(u_{1}, u_{2}, \ldots, u_{2023}\right)$ and $\mathbf{v}=\left(v_{1}, v_{2}, \ldots, v_{2023}\right)$, not necessarily distinct, from those she has already written, and then she also writes on the board the two 2023-tuples $\mathbf{u}+\mathbf{v}=\left(u_{1}+v_{1}, \ldots, u_{2023}+v_{2023}\right)$ and $\max (\mathbf{u}, \mathbf{v})=\left(\max \left(u_{1}, v_{1}\right), \ldots, \max \left(u_{2023}, v_{2023}\right)\right)$.
Let $m$ be the smallest positive integer $s$ such that, if Lucile judiciously chooses the $s$ 2023-tuples she initially writes, then by repeating the above operations she can eventually write any 2023-tuple of integers. Compute $m + 2023$.

Let $ABCD$ be a quadrilateral with an inscribed circle centered at $I$. Let $CI$ intersect $AB$ at $E$. If $\angle IDE = 35^\circ$, $\angle ABC = 70^\circ$, and $\angle BCD = 60^\circ$, find the sum of all possible measures, in degrees, of $\angle CDA$.

Mike and Harry play a game on an $8 \times 8$ board. For some positive integer $k$, Mike chooses $k$ squares and writes an $M$ in each of them. Harry then chooses $k+1$ squares and writes an $H$ in each of them. After Harry is done, Mike wins if there is a sequence of letters forming " $H M M$ " or " $M M H$," when read either horizontally or vertically, and Harry wins otherwise. Determine the smallest value of $k$ for which Mike has a winning strategy.

A mouse lives in a circular cage with completely reflective walls. At the edge of this cage, a small flashlight with vertex on the circle whose beam forms an angle of $15^{\circ}$ is centered at an angle of $37.5^{\circ}$ away from the center. The mouse will die in the dark. What fraction of the total area of the cage can keep the mouse alive?
![](https://cdn.mathpix.com/cropped/2025_01_24_143d587e7a2af30a2168g-1.jpg?height=370&width=370&top_left_y=2051&top_left_x=918)

Geometry Test

If the answer to this problem can be expressed as $\frac{p}{q}$ where $p$ and $q$ are coprime integers with $q > 0$, find $p + q$.
Hexagon $ABCDEF$ has both a circumscribed circle and an inscribed circle. Given that $AB=9$, $BC=6$, $CD=2$, and $EF=4$, find the value of $DE^3 + FA^3$.

Find the probability that the townspeople win if there are initially two townspeople and one goon.

If the answer to this problem can be expressed as $\frac{p}{q}$ where $p$ and $q$ are coprime integers with $q > 0$, find $p + q$.

Inside an equilateral triangle of side length 6 , three congruent equilateral triangles of side length $x$ with sides parallel to the original equilateral triangle are arranged so that each has a vertex on a side of the larger triangle, and a vertex on another one of the three equilateral triangles, as shown below.
![](https://cdn.mathpix.com/cropped/2025_01_24_24ae39a6021d1a1df482g-1.jpg?height=399&width=421&top_left_y=581&top_left_x=890)

A smaller equilateral triangle formed between the three congruent equilateral triangles has side length 1. Compute $x$.

If the answer to this problem can be expressed as $\frac{p}{q}$ where $p$ and $q$ are coprime integers with $q > 0$, find $p + q$.

Compute the number of ways to fill each of the 12 empty cells in the grid below with one of $T, A, L$, or $C$ such that each of the four rows, columns, and bolded $2 \times 2$ square regions contains each letter exactly once.
![](https://cdn.mathpix.com/cropped/2025_01_24_858c2c4f1409139ed214g-1.jpg?height=218&width=223&top_left_y=563&top_left_x=992)

A plane \(\mathcal{P}\) intersects a rectangular prism, forming a hexagonal cross-section. The sides of this hexagon, in consecutive order, have lengths 45, 66, 63, 55, 54, and 77. If the distance from the center of the rectangular prism to the plane \(\mathcal{P}\) can be expressed in the form \(\sqrt{\frac{p}{q}}\) where \(p\) and \(q\) are relatively prime positive integers, determine \(p+q\).

Find the largest possible radius of a circle that lies completely inside the region in the coordinate plane given by
\[
\left|\,x+\frac{4}{3}|y|\,\right|\le 136 .
\]

Equilateral triangle $ABC$ has side length $6$. Three squares $ABDE$, $BCFG$, and $CAHI$ are drawn externally to the triangle. The smallest triangle that contains these three squares has area of the form $a + b\sqrt{3}$, where $a$ and $b$ are integers. Find $a + b$.

10 people are playing musical chairs with $n$ chairs in a circle. They can be seated in 7 ! ways (assuming only one person fits on each chair, of course), where different arrangements of the same people on chairs, even rotations, are considered different. Find $n$.

19. (ITA 5) We are given a fixed point on the circle of radius 1, and going from this point along the circumference in the positive direction on curved distances $0,1,2, \ldots$ from it we obtain points with abscisas $n=0,1,2, \ldots$ respectively. How many points among them should we take to ensure that some two of them are less than the distance $1 / 5$ apart?

Let $S_{1}$ and $S_{2}$ be two spheres with distinct radii that touch externally. The spheres lie inside a cone $C$, and each sphere touches the cone in a full circle. Inside the cone there are $n$ additional solid spheres arranged in a ring in such a way that each solid sphere touches the cone $C$, both of the spheres $S_{1}$ and $S_{2}$ externally, as well as the two neighboring solid spheres. Determine the product of all positive integer values of $n$ for which such a configuration exists.

For a positive integer $r$, let $h(r)$ denote the smallest integer such that for any partition of the set $\{1,2,\dots,h(r)\}$ into $r$ classes, there exist integers $a\ge 0$, $1\le x\le y$ for which the numbers $a+x$, $a+y$, and $a+x+y$ all belong to the same class. Find $h(100)$.

6. C1 (UKR) On a $5 \times 5$ board, two players alternately mark numbers on empty cells. The first player always marks 1's, the second 0's. One number is marked per turn, until the board is filled. For each of the nine $3 \times 3$ squares the sum of the nine numbers on its cells is computed. Denote by $A$ the maximum of these sums. How large can the first player make $A$, regardless of the responses of the second player?

13. (BUL) ${ }^{\mathrm{IMO} 6}$ Determine the least possible value of $f(1998)$, where $f$ is a function from the set $\mathbb{N}$ of positive integers into itself such that for all $m, n \in \mathbb{N}$,  $$ f\left(n^{2} f(m)\right)=m[f(n)]^{2} $$

Let $p = 13$. Let $A$ be a set of positive integers that satisfies the following conditions:
(i) the set of prime divisors of the elements in $A$ consists of exactly $p-1$ primes;
(ii) for any nonempty subset of $A$, the product of its elements is not a perfect $p$-th power.
What is the largest possible number of elements in $A$?

Consider a matrix of size $202 \times 202$ whose entries are real numbers of absolute value not exceeding $1$, and the sum of all entries is $0$. Determine the least number $C$ such that every such matrix necessarily has a row or a column with the sum of its entries not exceeding $C$ in absolute value.

Let $k$ be a positive integer. Suppose $n$ distinct points are given on a line. For each pair of distinct points, we construct the circle having the segment between them as a diameter. Each circle is colored with one of $k$ colors. Define $f(k)$ to be the smallest positive integer $n$ such that, no matter how the circles are colored with $k$ colors, there always exist two circles of the same color that have a common external tangent. Determine $f(2024)$.

For a positive integer $n$, let $A_n$ be the set of all permutations $(a_1, a_2, \ldots, a_n)$ of the set $\{1,2,\ldots, n\}$ such that
\[
k \mid 2\left(a_1 + a_2 + \cdots + a_k\right) \quad \text{ for every } 1 \leqslant k \leqslant n.
\]
Find the number of elements in $A_{10}$.

On the planet $X$ in the shape of a sphere, there are $2 n$ gas stations. Each station is paired with one other station, and each pair of paired stations is located at diametrically opposite points on the planet. Each station has a certain amount of gasoline. The following is known: if a car with a previously empty (sufficiently large) tank starts from any station, it can always reach the station paired with it (with possible refueling at other stations along the way). Determine all natural numbers $n$ such that, for any arrangement of $2 n$ stations that satisfies the given condition, there is always a station from which a car can start with a previously empty tank and visit all other stations on the planet. Let $S$ be the set of all such $n$. Compute $\displaystyle\sum_{n \in S} n^5$.

Let $n=2$. Determine the number of ways to choose sets $S_{i j} \subseteq\{1,2,3,4\}$, for all $0 \leq i \leq 2$ and $0 \leq j \leq 2$ (not necessarily distinct), such that  
- $\left|S_{i j}\right|=i+j$, and  
- $S_{i j} \subseteq S_{k l}$ if $0 \leq i \leq k \leq 2$ and $0 \leq j \leq l \leq 2$.  
Express your answer as an integer.

Let $n = 100$. Find the smallest positive integer $k$ such that for any set $S$ of $n$ points in the interior of the unit square, there exists a set of $k$ rectangles such that the following hold:
- The sides of each rectangle are parallel to the sides of the unit square.
- Each point in $S$ is not in the interior of any rectangle.
- Each point in the interior of the unit square but not in $S$ is in the interior of at least one of the $k$ rectangles.
(The interior of a polygon does not contain its boundary.)

A tetrahedron \(ABCD\) is said to be angelic if it has nonzero volume and satisfies  

\[\angle BAC + \angle CAD + \angle DAB = \angle ABC + \angle CBD + \angle DBA,\] \[\angle ACB + \angle BCD + \angle DCA = \angle ADB + \angle BDC + \angle CDA.\]  

Across all angelic tetrahedrons, what is the maximum number of distinct lengths that could appear in the set \(\{AB, AC, AD, BC, BD, CD\}\) ?

Initially given $31$ tuplets
$$(1,0,0,\dots,0),(0,1,0,\dots,0),\dots, (0,0,0,\dots,1)$$  
were written on the blackboard. At every move we choose two written $31$ tuplets as $(a_1,a_2,a_3,\dots, a_{31})$ and $(b_1,b_2,b_3,\dots,b_{31})$, then write the $31$ tuplet $(a_1+b_1,a_2+b_2,a_3+b_3,\dots, a_{31}+b_{31})$ to the blackboard too. Find the least possible value of the moves such that one can write the $31$ tuplets
$$(0,1,1,\dots,1),(1,0,1,\dots,1),\dots, (1,1,1,\dots,0)$$  
to the blackboard by using those moves.

All integers from 1 to 100 are written in a string in an unknown order. With one question about any 50 numbers, you can find out the order of these 50 numbers relative to each other. What is the minimum number of questions needed to definitely find out the order of all 100 numbers?

#

Angelika owns a commercial space of $5$ square meters. She considers using it to open a music club where she would give piano lessons. However, a friend has offered her a job as a manager in his company. She wants to determine which option is more economically beneficial.

If she opens the club, Angelika plans to use the simplified tax system with a tax rate of $15\%$ of the profit. If she takes the job, her monthly net salary (after personal income tax) is $5000$ rubles, which she spends entirely on monthly expenses.

Additional information:
- The rent rate for similar commercial spaces is $1000$ rubles per square meter per year, payable at the beginning of the year.
- The interest rate on a loan is $12\%$ per year, with interest accrued at the end of the year.
- The interest rate on a deposit is $9\%$ per year, with interest accrued at the end of the year.

Determine the minimum annual profit (before taxation) that Angelika must achieve from the music club for this alternative to be economically beneficial compared to taking the job.

Jamie, a chronic pain patient, needs to take medication every 4 hours to manage their pain effectively. Jamie starts taking their medication at 7:00 AM and continues with this schedule throughout the day. Jamie's physician has asked them to keep a daily log of their medication intake to better understand the challenges they face with managing pain. If Jamie follows this schedule, how many times will they take their medication in a 24-hour period?

5.66 A deck of cards has a total of 54 cards. The magician divides them into several piles, and the audience writes a natural number on each card, which is equal to the number of cards in the pile where the card is located. Then the magician mixes the cards in a special way and divides them into several piles again. The audience writes a natural number on each card again, which is also equal to the number of cards in the pile where the card is now located. This process continues. How many times does this process of dividing piles and writing numbers need to be repeated at least, so that the (unordered) number arrays written on each card are all different?
Given the store's sales tax rate is 8%, the original price of the jacket is $120, and the promotional discount is 25%, calculate the difference between the total prices computed by Pete and Polly.

$15 \cdot 26$ Let the natural number $n(n>3)$ have the following property: when the set $S_{n}=\{3,4, \cdots, n\}$ is arbitrarily divided into two groups, there is always a group containing three numbers $a, b, c$ (allowing $a=b$), such that $a b=c$. Find the smallest value of such $n$.
(China National Training Team Test Question, 1988)
In a football match, the scoring rules are as follows: a win earns 3 points, a draw earns 1 point, and a loss earns 0 points. How many different ways can a team score 19 points in 14 matches?

Timur and Alexander are counting the trees growing around the house. Both move in the same direction, but they start counting from different trees. What is the number of trees growing around the house if the tree that Timur called the 12th, Alexander counted as $33-m$, and the tree that Timur called the $105-m$, Alexander counted as the 8th?

Let $n=10$. Determine the number of permutations $\left(a_{1}, \ldots, a_{10}\right)$ of the set $\{1,2, \ldots, 10\}$ with the following property:

\[ 
2\left(a_{1}+\ldots+a_{k}\right) \quad \text{is divisible by } k \quad \forall k \in\{1,2, \ldots, 10\} 
\]

Compute this number.

On a line, 100 points are marked, and one additional point is marked outside the line. Consider all the triangles with vertices at these points.

What is the maximum number of them that can be isosceles?

Andrew the Antelope canters along the surface of a regular icosahedron, which has twenty equilateral triangle faces and edge length 4. (A three-dimensional image of an icosahedron is shown to the right.) If he wants to move from one vertex to the opposite vertex, the minimum distance he must travel can be expressed as $\sqrt{n}$ for some integer $n$. Compute $n$.
12. As shown in Figure 7, $\triangle ABD$ and $\triangle CED$ are both equilateral triangles, $AC = BC$, and $AC \perp BC$. If $BE = 6\sqrt{2}$, compute $\left(CD + \frac{1}{2} AB\right)^2$.

$n$ players participate in a chess tournament where each player plays a game with every other player. The winner of a game receives 1 point, the loser receives 0 points, and a draw awards each player 0.5 points. A tournament is said to have property $P(52)$ if, among any $52$ players, there is one player who has defeated the other $51$ players, and there is one player who has lost to the other $51$ players. Find the minimum value of $n$ such that in any tournament with property $P(52)$, all $n$ players have different scores.

Alex starts at the origin O of a hexagonal lattice. Every second, he moves to one of the six vertices adjacent to the vertex he is currently at. If he ends up at X after 2018 moves, then let p be the probability that the shortest walk from O to X (where a valid move is from a vertex to an adjacent vertex) has length 2018. Then p can be expressed as $\frac{a \cdot b^m}{c^n}$, where a, b, and c are positive integers less than 10; a and c are not perfect squares; and m and n are positive integers less than 10000. Find a + b + c + m + n.

A cat is tied to one corner of the base of a tower. The base forms an equilateral triangle of side length 4 m, and the cat is tied with a leash of length 8 m. Let A be the area of the region accessible to the cat. If we write $A = \frac{m}{n}\pi - k\sqrt{l}$, where m, n, k, l are positive integers such that m and n are relatively prime, and l is squarefree, what is the value of m + n + k + l?

Two spheres with radii 6 and 12 are in contact (externally tangent). They have a common tangent cone. These three surfaces divide space into several regions. Exactly one of these regions is bounded by all three surfaces; it is ring-shaped. Find the volume of this ring-shaped region. If the volume is \(V = k\pi\) for some integer \(k\), determine \(k\).

Let $M$ be the midpoint of side $BC$ of a general $\triangle ABC$. Using the smallest possible $n$, describe a method for cutting $\triangle AMB$ into $n$ triangles which can be reassembled to form a triangle congruent to $\triangle AMC$ and return this value of $n$.

An ellipse with semi-axes lengths $a$ and $b$ rolls without slipping on the curve $y = c \sin\left(\frac{x}{a}\right)$. It is observed that when the ellipse travels exactly one period of the curve, it makes exactly one complete revolution. Given that $a=120$ and $c=119$, determine the value of $b$.

Every day at noon, a mail steamer leaves from Le Havre to New York, and at the same time, another steamer from the same company leaves New York for Le Havre. Each of these steamers takes exactly seven days to complete their journey, and they travel the same route.

How many steamers from the same company will a steamer traveling from Le Havre to New York meet on its way?

In the following diagram, two lines that meet at a point \( A \) are tangent to a circle at points \( B \) and \( C \). The line parallel to \( AC \) passing through \( B \) meets the circle again at \( D \). Join the segments \( CD \) and \( AD \). Suppose \( AB = 49 \) and \( CD = 28 \). Determine the length of \( AD \).

A convex quadrilateral \(EFGH\) has vertices \(E, F, G, H\) lying respectively on the sides \(AB, BC, CD,\) and \(DA\) of another quadrilateral \(ABCD\). It satisfies the equation \(\frac{AE}{EB} \cdot \frac{BF}{FC} \cdot \frac{CG}{GD} \cdot \frac{DH}{HA} = 1\). Given that points \(E, F, G,\) and \(H\) lie on the sides of quadrilateral \(E_1F_1G_1H_1\) respectively with \(\frac{E_1A}{AH_1} = \lambda\), find the value of \(\frac{F_1C}{CG_1}\).
Find the smallest natural number in which each digit appears exactly once and that is divisible by 990.

Mr. Stevens, a businessman, owned and operated a small retail shop in Boone Mall from 1995 to 2015. During his first year in business, he sold 1,200 items. Over the next 10 years, his sales increased by 150 items each year. In his final year of business, he decided to have a closing sale and managed to sell 2,000 items. How many items in total did Mr. Stevens sell from 1995 to 2015?

A podcast host records an episode with Dave Franco, which lasts for 90 minutes. During the first 30 minutes, they discuss Dave's early career, followed by a 15-minute segment about his creative process. The remaining time is dedicated to discussing his recent projects. If the host wants to include 3 commercial breaks of equal duration throughout the episode, how long is each commercial break in minutes?

A point-sized cue ball is fired from the center of a regular hexagonal billiards table with side length $1$. If it is not aimed directly at a pocket but travels an integer distance before falling into a pocket (located at the corners), find the minimum distance it could have traveled.
For which integers  $n>1$  does there exist a rectangle that can be subdivided into  $n$  pairwise noncongruent rectangles similar to the original rectangle?

Compute the largest possible number of distinct real solutions for  $x$  to the equation \[x^6+ax^5+60x^4-159x^3+240x^2+bx+c=0,\] where  $a$ ,  $b$ , and  $c$  are real numbers.

Given that
\[
\cos^2 \alpha \sin^2 \beta + \sin^2 \alpha \cos^2 \beta = \cos \alpha \sin \alpha \cos \beta \sin \beta,
\]
find the value of
\[
\frac{\sin^2 \beta \cos^2 \alpha}{\sin^2 \alpha} + \frac{\cos^2 \beta \sin^2 \alpha}{\cos^2 \alpha}.
\]
Let $n$ be a positive integer and $a,b,c,d$ be integers such that $a\equiv c^{-1} \pmod{n}$ and $b\equiv d^{-1} \pmod{n}$. What is the remainder when $(ab + cd)$ is divided by $n$?

A bicycle travels due north at $\frac{1}{2}$ mile per minute on a straight path. Simultaneously, a circular fog bank with a radius of $40$ miles moves northeast at $\frac{1}{3}\sqrt{2}$ mile per minute. At time $t=0$, the center of the fog is $100$ miles due east of the bicycle. Determine $\frac{1}{2}(t_1+t_2)$, where $t_1$ and $t_2$ are the times when the bicycle enters and leaves the fog bank, respectively.
Let $p<q<r$ be three integers such that $p,q,r$ is a geometric progression and $p,r,q$ is an arithmetic progression. Find the smallest possible value of $r$.
Given three non-zero real numbers \(a, b, c\) such that the equations \(a x^{2}+b x+c=0\), \(b x^{2}+c x+a=0\), \(c x^{2}+a x+b=0\) each have two roots. How many of these roots can be negative?

In a math competition, the possible scores for each problem for each participating team are 0 points, 3 points, or 5 points. By the end of the competition, the sum of the total scores of three teams is 32 points. If the total score of any single team can reach 32 points, how many different possible combinations are there for the total scores of these three teams?

The lateral faces of a pentagonal pyramid \( S A B C D E \) are acute-angled triangles. We will call a lateral edge of the pyramid good if it is equal to the height of the opposite lateral face, drawn from the apex of the pyramid. For example, edge \( S A \) is good if it is equal to the height of triangle \( S C D \), drawn from vertex \( S \). What is the maximum number of good edges that the pyramid can have?

A and B play a number-changing game on a $5 \times 5$ grid: A starts and both take turns filling empty spaces, with A filling each space with the number 1 and B filling each space with the number 0. After the grid is completely filled, the sum of the numbers in each $3 \times 3$ square is calculated, and the maximum sum among these squares is denoted as $A$. A tries to maximize $A$, while B tries to minimize $A$. What is the maximum value of $A$ that A can achieve? 

(The problem is from the 35th IMO selection test)

Color 101 cells blue in an $n \times n$ grid. It is known that there is a unique way to cut the grid along square lines into rectangles such that each rectangle contains exactly one blue cell. Find the smallest possible value of $n$.

Divide the set \( M = \{1, 2, \ldots, 12\} \) of the first 12 positive integers into four subsets each containing three elements, such that in each subset, one number is the sum of the other two. Find the number of different ways to do this.

Among five externally identical coins, 3 are genuine and 2 are counterfeit, with the counterfeits weighing the same but it is unknown whether they are heavier or lighter than the genuine coins. How can you find at least one genuine coin with the fewest possible weighings?
The pentagon \(ABCDE\) is inscribed around a circle. The angles at its vertices \(A\), \(C\), and \(E\) are \(100^{\circ}\). Find the angle \(ACE\).

Each face of a $6 \times 6 \times 6$ cube is divided into $1 \times 1$ cells. The cube is covered with $2 \times 2$ squares such that each square covers exactly four cells, no squares overlap, and each cell is covered by an equal number of squares. What is the maximum value of this equal number? (A square can be folded over an edge.)

There are 3 piles of stones. Each time, person A moves 1 stone from one pile to another. Each time A moves a stone, they receive a reward from person B. The amount of money A receives is equal to the difference between the number of stones in the pile to which they added the stone and the number of stones in the pile from which the stone was taken. If this difference is negative, person A must return that amount of money to person B (if A does not have enough money to return, they can owe it temporarily). After several moves, all the stones return to their original piles. Find the maximum amount of money A can earn.
Evaluate $$\frac{1}{\sqrt{1+\sqrt{2}}} + \frac{1}{\sqrt{2+\sqrt{3}}} + \cdots + \frac{1}{\sqrt{1368+\sqrt{1369}}}.$$

Consider the following molecules: $\mathrm{Br}_{3} \mathrm{O}_{8}, \mathrm{~F}_{2} \mathrm{O}, \mathrm{H}_{2} \mathrm{~S}_{4} \mathrm{O}_{6}, \mathrm{H}_{2} \mathrm{~S}_{5} \mathrm{O}_{6}$, and $\mathrm{C}_{3} \mathrm{O}_{2}$.



Count the number of atoms existing in their zero oxidation state in each molecule. What is their sum?

9. (40 points) Among nine visually identical gold coins, one weighs $a$, seven weigh $b$, and the last one weighs $c$, and $a < b < c$. Using a balance scale, find the minimum number of weighings required to identify the coin weighing $a$ and the coin weighing $c$.

To solve this problem, we need to devise a strategy to identify the coins with weights $a$ and $c$ using the fewest number of weighings. Here is a step-by-step approach:

1. **First Weighing:**
   - Divide the nine coins into three groups of three coins each: Group 1, Group 2, and Group 3.
   - Weigh Group 1 against Group 2.

   **Case 1:** If Group 1 and Group 2 balance, then the coin weighing $a$ and the coin weighing $c$ must be in Group 3.
   - Weigh two coins from Group 3 against each other.
     - If they balance, the remaining coin in Group 3 is the one weighing $c$.
     - If they do not balance, the lighter coin is the one weighing $a$ and the heavier coin is the one weighing $c$.

   **Case 2:** If Group 1 and Group 2 do not balance, then the coin weighing $a$ and the coin weighing $c$ are in the lighter and heavier groups, respectively.
   - Identify the lighter group (Group 1 or Group 2) and the heavier group (Group 1 or Group 2).
   - Weigh two coins from the lighter group against each other.
     - If they balance, the remaining coin in the lighter group is the one weighing $a$.
     - If they do not balance, the lighter coin is the one weighing $a$.
   - Weigh two coins from the heavier group against each other.
     - If they balance, the remaining coin in the heavier group is the one weighing $c$.
     - If they do not balance, the heavier coin is the one weighing $c$.

In both cases, we can identify the coins weighing $a$ and $c$ in a minimum of 2 weighings.

Thus, the minimum number of weighings required is \(\boxed{2}\).

A measurement complex \(M\) integrated into an industrial process transmits to a transmission unit \(A_{1}\) exactly one of the two signals \(S_{1}\) or \(S_{2}\), which is then transmitted from \(A_{1}\) to a transmission unit \(A_{2}\), from \(A_{2}\) to a transmission unit \(A_{3}\), and from \(A_{3}\) to an electronic computer \(R\).

Each transmission unit \(A_{i} (i=1,2,3)\) can transmit exactly the signals \(S_{1}\) or \(S_{2}\). The probability that \(A_{i}\) transmits the other signal instead of the one it received is 0.01.

It is now known that at the end of such a process, transmitted through \(A_{3}\) to the computer \(R\), the signal \(S_{1}\) was transmitted.

What is the probability that \(M\) transmitted \(S_{1}\) to \(A_{1}\) at the beginning of this process?

Hint:

If under certain conditions \(V\), in a large number \(n\) of cases, a total of \(g\) cases occur in which an event \(E\) occurs or has occurred, then the number \(p=\frac{g}{n}\) is the probability of the occurrence (or having occurred) of \(E\) under the conditions \(V\).

For the solution, the following theorems can also be used.

a) Addition rule of probability for independent events: The probability that one of two mutually exclusive events \(E_{1}\) and \(E_{2}\) occurs is equal to the sum \(p_{1}+p_{2}\) of the probability \(p_{1}\) of the occurrence of \(E_{1}\) and the probability \(p_{2}\) of the occurrence of \(E_{2}\).

b) Multiplication rule of probability: The probability that an event \(E\) and an event \(F\) occur is equal to the product \(p \cdot q\) of the probability \(p\) of the occurrence of \(E\) and the probability \(q\) that \(F\) occurs given \(E\).

Example 5 Given the quadratic equation in $x$
$$
\left(k^{2}-8 k+15\right) x^{2}-2(13-3 k) x+8=0
$$

both roots are integers. Find the value of the real number $k$.
Analysis: Since $k$ is a real number, we cannot solve it using the discriminant. We can first find the two roots of the equation $x_{1}=$ $\frac{2}{5-k}, x_{2}=\frac{4}{3-k}$. Since $x_{1} 、 x_{2}$ are integers, we can eliminate $k$ from the above two equations to obtain an indeterminate equation about $x_{1} 、 x_{2}$. Solving for $x_{1} 、 x_{2}$, we can then find $k$.

Example 3. Integrate the differential equation

$$
\left(1+x^{2}\right) d y-2 x y d x=0
$$

Find a particular solution that satisfies the condition: $y=1$ when $x=0$. Solution. The given equation is a separable equation (the coefficient of $d y$ is a function of $x$ only, and the coefficient of $d x$ is a product of functions, one depending only on $x$ and the other only on $y$). Dividing both sides of the equation by the product $y\left(1+x^{2}\right)$, we obtain an equation with separated variables

$$
\frac{d y}{y}-\frac{2 x d x}{1+x^{2}}=0
$$

Integrating this equation, we find

$$
\ln |y|-\ln \left(1+x^{2}\right)=\ln |C|
$$

or

$$
\ln \left(\frac{|y|}{1+x^{2}}\right)=\ln |C|
$$

from which we obtain the general solution

$$
y=C\left(1+x^{2}\right)
$$

To find the required particular solution, it is sufficient to determine the value of $C$ using the initial conditions:

$$
1=C(1+0), C=1
$$

Thus, the particular solution is

$$
y=1+x^{2}
$$

Remark. When dividing by $y\left(1+x^{2}\right)$, it was assumed that $y(1+x^{2}) \neq 0$, i.e., $y \neq 0, 1+x^{2} \neq 0$. However, $y=0$ is a solution of the equation, which can be verified directly. This solution is obtained from the general solution when $C=0$.

146. Count how many different $p$-arithmetic fractional-linear functions there are.

The function $f(f(x))$ is denoted by $f_{2}(x)$. Similarly, we introduce fractional-linear functions $f_{\mathrm{B}}(x), f_{1}(x), \ldots, f_{2}(x)$, assuming

$$
\begin{aligned}
f_{3}(x) & =f\left(f_{2}(x)\right), \\
f_{4}(x) & =f\left(f_{\mathrm{B}}(x)\right), \\
\cdots & \cdot \\
f_{n}(x) & =f\left(f_{n-1}(x)\right) .
\end{aligned}
$$

For example,

$$
\begin{aligned}
& f(x)=\frac{x+1}{x} \\
& f_{2}(x)=\frac{\frac{x+1}{x}+1}{\frac{x+1}{x}}=\frac{2 x+1}{x+1} \\
& f_{3}(x)=\frac{\frac{2 x+1}{x+1}+1}{\frac{2 x+1}{x+1}}=\frac{3 x+1}{2 x+1}
\end{aligned}
$$

The action of all functions $f_{n}(x)$ can be traced on a diagram constructed for the function $f(x)$. The action of the function $f(x)$ is such that each point of its diagram moves to the next one, i.e., makes one step in the direction of the arrows. When applying the function $f_{2}(x)$, each point on the diagram of $f(x)$ already makes two steps, landing in the second point. Generally, when applying $f_{n}(x)$, each point on the diagram of $f(x)$ makes $n$ steps in the direction of the arrows, jumping over $n-1$ points to the $n$-th. This allows constructing the diagrams of the functions $f_{2}(x), f_{3}(x), \ldots$ from the diagram of the function $f(x)$ without calculations.

A natural number's square consists of 202 digits. The first 100 digits are 1s, followed by 101 digits of 2s. Determine the last digit and the number.

Let's solve this problem step by step.

1. **Understanding the Problem:**
   - The square of a natural number has 202 digits.
   - The first 100 digits are 1s.
   - The next 101 digits are 2s.

2. **Formulating the Number:**
   - The number can be represented as \( N^2 \), where \( N \) is the natural number we need to find.
   - The number \( N^2 \) looks like \( 111\ldots111222\ldots222 \) (100 ones followed by 101 twos).

3. **Finding the Last Digit:**
   - To find the last digit of \( N^2 \), we need to consider the last digit of \( N \).
   - The last digit of \( N^2 \) is determined by the last digit of \( N \).

4. **Possible Last Digits of \( N \):**
   - The last digit of \( N \) can be 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, or 9.
   - We need to check which of these, when squared, end in 2.

5. **Checking Each Case:**
   - \( 0^2 = 0 \)
   - \( 1^2 = 1 \)
   - \( 2^2 = 4 \)
   - \( 3^2 = 9 \)
   - \( 4^2 = 16 \) (last digit is 6)
   - \( 5^2 = 25 \) (last digit is 5)
   - \( 6^2 = 36 \) (last digit is 6)
   - \( 7^2 = 49 \) (last digit is 9)
   - \( 8^2 = 64 \) (last digit is 4)
   - \( 9^2 = 81 \) (last digit is 1)

   None of these squares end in 2. Therefore, the last digit of \( N \) must be such that when squared, it ends in 2. This is not possible with the digits 0 through 9.

6. **Conclusion:**
   - Since no single digit squared ends in 2, the problem as stated has no solution in the realm of natural numbers.

Therefore, the problem as stated does not have a valid solution. If there is additional context or a different interpretation, please provide it.

- Dividends from shares of the company PAO “Winning” amounted to 50,000 rubles.
- Coupon income from government bonds OFZ amounted to 40,000 rubles.
- Coupon income from corporate bonds of PAO “Reliable” amounted to 30,000 rubles.

In addition, the investor received a capital gain from selling 100 shares of PAO "Risky" at 200 rubles per share. The purchase price was 150 rubles per share. The investor held the shares for 4 months.

Calculate the amount of personal income tax (NDFL) on the income from the securities.
A worker's salary is reduced by 30%. What percentage increase is needed on the new salary to restore it to the original salary?
The graph of $y^2 + 2xy + 25|x| = 625$ partitions the plane into several regions. Calculate the volume of the solid formed by extending the bounded region vertically to a height of $h = 10$ units.

Initially, there were twenty states that could opt to change their primary energy source to solar. If fifteen states decide to go ahead, and two later revert to their previous energy sources, what will be the new ratio rounded to the nearest tenth?

In a certain meeting, there are 30 participants. Each person knows at most 5 others among the remaining participants, and in any group of 5 people, there are always two who do not know each other. Find the largest positive integer \( k \) such that there exists a subset of \( k \) people from these 30 people who do not know each other.

A regular hexagon $ABCDEF$ with side length 2 has two circles positioned outside it. The first circle is tangent to $\overline{AB}$ and the second circle is tangent to $\overline{CD}$. Both circles are also tangent to lines $BC$ and $FA$. Find the ratio of the area of the second circle to that of the first circle.

Let \( f(x) = x^2 - r_2 x + r_3 \) for all real numbers \( x \), where \( r_2 \) and \( r_3 \) are some real numbers. Define a sequence \( \{ g_n \} \) for all nonnegative integers \( n \) by \( g_0 = 0 \) and \( g_{n+1} = f(g_n) \). Assume that \( \{ g_n \} \) satisfies the following three conditions:
1. \( g_{2i} < g_{2i+1} \) and \( g_{2i+1} > g_{2i+2} \) for all \( 0 \leq i \leq 2011 \),
2. There exists a positive integer \( j \) such that \( g_{i+1} > g_i \) for all \( i > j \),
3. \( \{ g_n \} \) is unbounded.

If \( A \) is the greatest number such that \( A \leq |r_2| \) for any function \( f \) satisfying these properties, find \( A \).

Mr. Carter is a construction company owner who believes that installing solar panels is too costly and impractical. He is currently working on a project to build 10 houses. If he decides to incorporate solar panels into each house, the cost of solar panels per house is $12,000. Additionally, the installation of solar panels would save $1,000 per year on electricity bills for each house. 

Mr. Carter estimates that the houses will be sold after 5 years. Calculate the total cost of installing solar panels for all 10 houses and determine the total amount of money saved on electricity bills over 5 years for all 10 houses. How much money would Mr. Carter effectively save or spend by incorporating solar panels when considering the electricity savings over 5 years?

A retired history teacher who lives in the former Berwick area, now divided into South Berwick and North Berwick, decides to visit both towns to deliver history talks. On Monday, the teacher travels from South Berwick to North Berwick, a distance of 5 miles, and delivers a talk at the local library. On Tuesday, the teacher travels back to South Berwick to give another talk at the community center, which is another 5 miles. On Wednesday, the teacher visits a museum in South Berwick and walks 2 miles to and from the museum. On Thursday, the teacher goes to North Berwick again for a special history event, traveling another 5 miles one way. How many total miles did the retired history teacher travel by the end of Thursday?

The museum curator is organizing a special exhibition that features a portrait titled "The Vendor's Spirit," which symbolizes resilience and inclusion. The exhibition will have 5 different sections, each highlighting a different aspect of resilience or inclusion. The curator decides that each section will showcase 3 portraits, including "The Vendor's Spirit," which will be displayed in all sections as the centerpiece. 

If each portrait, including "The Vendor's Spirit," costs $200 to frame, and the museum already has 10 frames available for free, how much will the museum spend on framing all the portraits needed for the exhibition?
The following bar graph represents the length (in letters) of the names of 19 people. What is the median length of these names?

The average age of 40 fifth-graders is 10 years. The average age of 60 of their parents is 35 years. Additionally, there are 10 teachers with an average age of 45 years. What is the average age of all these fifth-graders, parents, and teachers combined?

A sphere is inscribed in a dihedral angle.

The sphere with center at point \( O \) touches the planes \( A^{\prime} B^{\prime} C^{\prime} \) and \( A A^{\prime} B \) and does not intersect the plane \( A A^{\prime} D \). Find the distance from point \( O \) to this plane.

All three-digit numbers from 100 to 999 are written consecutively without spaces. Kostya underlined $k$ consecutive digits in this sequence, and Andrey underlined another $k$ consecutive digits in this sequence. The $k$-digit numbers underlined by the boys are equal. What is the largest possible value of $k$ for which this could happen?

Liam lives in Larne, Northern Ireland, and frequently travels to the Isle of Man for work. The ferry from Larne to the Isle of Man takes 2 hours and 45 minutes one way. Liam makes this trip twice a week. Last month, Liam traveled to the Isle of Man every week and spent an additional 5 hours each week working on the island. 

How many hours in total did Liam spend traveling to and working on the Isle of Man last month, assuming last month had 4 weeks?

The doctoral student is studying the economic history of a small town during the Industrial Revolution. They are analyzing the growth of a local factory that started with 50 workers in the year 1850. Each year, the factory hired 10 more workers. By the year 1855, the factory also started producing a new product, which increased its workforce by an additional 5 workers each year. How many workers did the factory have by the end of the year 1860?

Alex has a rare phobia of balloons popping, called globophobia. To overcome their fear, Alex decides to take small steps by gradually exposing themselves to balloons in a controlled setting. On the first day, Alex bravely handles 3 balloons. Each day, they increase the number of balloons by 2 more than the previous day. If Alex continues this pattern for a total of 7 days, how many balloons does Alex handle on the seventh day?

Alex is a professional athlete who has been training for another bodybuilding competition. As part of their daily routine, Alex does 4 sets of exercises, with each set consisting of 15 repetitions. Each repetition burns 12 calories. After the exercises, Alex drinks a protein shake that contains 180 calories. If Alex consumes a total of 2,500 calories each day, how many calories does Alex have left for other meals after completing the exercises and drinking the protein shake?

There were several whole heads of cheese stored in a warehouse. During the night, some rats came and ate 10 heads, with each rat eating an equal amount. Some of the rats got sick from overeating. The remaining seven rats came the next night and finished the leftover cheese, but each rat could only eat half as much cheese as they did the night before. How much cheese was originally stored in the warehouse?

An ambitious young woman named Aisha grew up in the small town of Allipur and recently moved to a large city to attend university. In Allipur, Aisha used to walk 2 kilometers to her local library every week. Now, in the city, the university library is 5 kilometers from her apartment, but she can use a bicycle to travel.

Aisha wants to know how much more distance she covers each month if she visits the library twice a week in the city compared to her weekly visits in Allipur. Calculate the additional distance Aisha travels in a month (consider a month to have 4 weeks) now that she is in the city.

How many more kilometers does Aisha travel each month in the city compared to Allipur?

Professor Zhang at Shanxi Technology and Business College has been guiding students through their academic journey for 10 years. Each year, he mentors 5 new students. By the end of each year, 3 of his previously mentored students graduate and he remains in contact with 2 of them. After 10 years, how many of Professor Zhang's former students does he still keep in contact with?

The owner of an art restoration studio, Ms. Lee, offers apprenticeships to recent art school graduates. Each apprentice works on restoring paintings under her guidance. The studio has received 15 paintings for restoration this month. Ms. Lee has 3 apprentices working in her studio. Each apprentice can restore 2 paintings per week. If Ms. Lee wants all the paintings restored by the end of the month, which is 4 weeks from now, will the apprentices be able to complete the task on time? If not, how many additional paintings will Ms. Lee need to restore herself to meet the deadline?

Calculate the amount of personal income tax (НДФЛ) paid by Sergey over the past year if he is a resident of the Russian Federation and had a stable income of 30,000 rubles per month and a one-time vacation bonus of 20,000 rubles during this period. Last year, Sergey sold his car, which he inherited two years ago, for 250,000 rubles and bought a plot of land for building a house for 300,000 rubles. Sergey applied all applicable tax deductions. (Provide the answer without spaces and units of measurement.)
Given seven positive consecutive integers starting with $c$, find the average of seven consecutive integers starting with $d$, where $d$ is the average of the first set of integers.

A sample is divided into 5 groups, with a total of 160 data points in the first, second, and third groups, and a total of 260 data points in the third, fourth, and fifth groups, and the frequency of the third group is 0.20. Calculate the frequency of the third group.

The number of elderly employees in a sample of 32 young employees from a workplace with a total of 430 employees, 160 of whom are young and the number of middle-aged employees is twice the number of elderly employees, can be found by determining the ratio of young employees in the population and the sample.
The product underwent a price reduction from 25 yuan to 16 yuan. Calculate the average percentage reduction for each price reduction.
Given that Sarah had the capacity to paint 45 rooms and 4 cans of paint were dropped, determine the number of cans of paint used to paint 35 rooms.
Compute the difference between Mark's total and Mary's total bill for a coat originally priced at $120.00, which is being sold at a 25% discount, when the sales tax rate is 7%.

Lina is an aspiring scientist from a country where the esteemed feminist historian, Dr. Maria, is highly celebrated for her work in promoting gender equality. Inspired by Dr. Maria, Lina decides to conduct a small survey on how many hours students spend on science and history subjects each week. She gathers data from 5 students and records the following hours for each subject:

- Student 1: 6 hours on science, 4 hours on history
- Student 2: 7 hours on science, 5 hours on history
- Student 3: 5 hours on science, 3 hours on history
- Student 4: 8 hours on science, 6 hours on history
- Student 5: 4 hours on science, 2 hours on history

Dr. Maria suggests that a balanced schedule should have a total of 10 hours per week combining both subjects. Lina wants to find out how many more hours the students need to invest collectively to achieve Dr. Maria's suggested balance.

Calculate the total number of additional hours all 5 students together need to spend on science and history to reach the balanced 10-hour schedule per student per week.

A magical checkered sheet of paper of size $2000 \times 70$, initially has all cells grey. A painter stands on a certain cell and paints it red. Every second, the painter makes two steps: one cell to the left and one cell down, and paints the cell he lands on red. If the painter is in the leftmost column and needs to step left, he teleports to the rightmost cell of the same row; if the painter is in the bottom row and needs to step down, he teleports to the top cell of the same column. After several moves, the painter returns to the cell where he started. How many cells have been painted red at this point?

A rancher owns a piece of land adjacent to a protected area. The rancher's property is rectangular and measures 120 meters along one side that borders the protected land, and 80 meters along the adjacent side. The rancher needs to build a fence along the two sides that do not border the protected land. If the cost of materials is $15 per meter of fencing, how much will it cost the rancher to build the fence?

Lara in her car notices Leo on his motorcycle $1$ mile ahead moving in the same direction. After she overtakes him, she can still see him in her rearview mirror until he is $1$ mile behind her. Lara drives at a constant speed of $60$ miles per hour, and Leo cruises at a constant speed of $40$ miles per hour. Calculate the time in minutes that Lara can see Leo.

In an aquarium, there are three types of fish: goldfish, silverfish, and red fish. If a cat eats all the goldfish, then the number of fish will be 1 less than $\frac{2}{3}$ of the original number. If the cat eats all the red fish, then the number of fish will be 4 more than $\frac{2}{3}$ of the original number. Which type of fish—goldfish or silverfish—is more numerous, and by how much?

The Debate Club at Lincoln Middle School consists of 12 members who are all public speaking enthusiasts. They meet every week to prepare for their upcoming debate competitions. Each debate session lasts for 1 hour and 30 minutes. This month, they have scheduled 4 debate sessions. During each session, they split into 3 groups to practice. Each group debates for an equal amount of time during the session, and each member gets the same amount of speaking time. 

How many minutes does each member get to speak in total during all the debate sessions this month?
Given Suzanna rides her bike at a constant rate as shown by a graph, if she rides for 40 minutes at the same speed, how many miles would she have ridden?

Given that the monogram consists of three initials in alphabetical order with a last initial of 'X', and the first and middle initials must be distinct, determine the total number of possible monograms.

Mr. Johnson is a retired teacher who actively attends union meetings to support his fellow educators. Last month, he attended 5 different union meetings. At each meeting, he brought along 3 retired friends to also show their support. If each meeting lasted 2 hours, and they spent an additional 30 minutes in discussions after each meeting, how many total hours did Mr. Johnson and his friends spend attending and discussing union meetings last month?

For a certain weekend, the weatherman predicts that it will rain with a $60\%$ probability on Saturday and a $40\%$ probability on Sunday. If it rains on Saturday, the probability that it will also rain on Sunday increases to $80\%$. Calculate the probability that it rains on at least one day over the weekend. Express your answer as a percentage.

Given that each licence candy costs $24$ cents, calculate the smallest possible value of $n$ when Casper has exactly enough money to buy $10$ pieces of jelly candies, $16$ pieces of chocolate candies, or $18$ pieces of gummies.

Mr. Thompson is a computer science educator who insists that his students submit their assignments on paper. Each week, he teaches three classes with 25 students each. Every student must submit a 5-page paper assignment. Mr. Thompson needs to staple all the pages together before grading. He uses a stapler that can hold 50 staples at a time. 

How many times will Mr. Thompson need to refill his stapler to staple all the assignments for one week?
Evaluate the expression $-20 + 15 \times (4^{\div -1} \times 2)$.
If an odd square not divisible by 9 is decreased by one, the result is divisible by 24.
Here is a fairly simple puzzle: EH is four times greater than OY. AY is four times greater than OH. Find the sum of all four.

The Wolf and the three little pigs wrote a detective story "The Three Little Pigs-2", and then, together with Little Red Riding Hood and her grandmother, a cookbook "Little Red Riding Hood-2". The publisher gave the fee for both books to the pig Naf-Naf. He took his share and handed the remaining 2100 gold coins to the Wolf. The fee for each book is divided equally among its authors. How much money should the Wolf take for himself?

For which positive natural numbers  $n$ , for every divisor  $t$  of  $n$ , that  $d (t)$  is a divisor of  $d (n)$ ?

A large circular pizza dough has a radius of 4 inches. Nine mini-pizzas of radius 1 inch each are cut from it, all touching each other and the edge, except the central mini-pizza. What is the radius of the reshaped mini-pizza?

Given that Big Al, the ape, ate 140 bananas from May 1 through May 6, with each day's total being five more than the previous day, but on May 4 he did not eat any, calculate the number of bananas Big Al ate on May 6.

Given that Liam bought some pencils costing more than a penny each at the school bookstore and paid $\textdollar 2.10$, and Mia bought some of the same pencils and paid $\textdollar 2.82$, determine the number of pencils that Mia bought compared to Liam.
Bob ate a total of 55 muffins in four days. Each day after the first day he ate two more muffins than he had eaten on the previous day. How many muffins did Bob eat on the second day?
Find the sum of the base 6 values $5_6 + 7_6 + 9_6 + \cdots + 31_6$. Express your answer in base 6.

The curve $y = \sin x$ intersects with the line $y = \sin 60^\circ$ on a coordinate plane. Determine the ordered pair of relatively prime positive integers $(p, q)$ that represents the ratio of the segments created by these intersections, assuming $p < q$.
Calculate the sum of the digits of the product of the base eight numbers $35_8$ and $42_8$, and express the result in base ten.
Suppose $\sin N = \frac{3}{5}$ in a right triangle LMN, where LM is 15 units. What is the length of LN?
In the right-angled triangle $LMN$, suppose $\sin N = \frac{3}{5}$. If the length of $LM$ is 15, calculate the length of $LN$.

Genevieve wants to further promote her school's annual Kite Olympics by making yet another large kite. This time, she designs it by quintupling both the height and width dimensions of the original small kite on a grid where points are one inch apart. Specifically, the quadrilateral extends for a base length of 35 inches (quintupling the original 7 inches) and a height of 15 inches from the mid-point (quintupling the original 3 inches). What is the area in square inches of this new large kite?

Over the course of three years, Marina did not invest the funds in her Individual Investment Account (IIA) into financial instruments and therefore did not receive any income from it. However, she gained the right to an investment tax deduction for depositing her own money into the IIA.

The tax deduction is provided for the amount of money deposited into the IIA during the tax period, but not more than 400,000 rubles in total per year.

Marina is entitled to receive 13% of the amount deposited into the IIA as a refund of the Personal Income Tax (PIT) that she paid on her income.

The PIT amount deducted from Marina's annual salary is equal to \( 30,000 \text{ rubles} \times 12 \text{ months} \times 0.13 = 46,800 \text{ rubles} \).

The tax deduction for the first year is \( 100,000 \text{ rubles} \times 0.13 = 13,000 \text{ rubles} \). This amount does not exceed the PIT deducted from Marina's annual salary.

The tax deduction for the second year is \( 400,000 \text{ rubles} \times 0.13 = 52,000 \text{ rubles} \). This amount exceeds the PIT deducted from Marina's annual salary. Therefore, the tax deduction will be limited to the PIT paid for the second year, or 46,800 rubles.

The tax deduction for the third year is \( 400,000 \text{ rubles} \times 0.13 = 52,000 \text{ rubles} \). This amount also exceeds the PIT deducted from Marina's annual salary. Therefore, the tax deduction will be limited to the PIT paid for the third year, or 46,800 rubles.

The total amount of tax deduction for 3 years is \( 13,000 + 46,800 + 46,800 = 106,600 \text{ rubles} \).

The return on Marina's transactions over 3 years is \( \frac{106,600}{1,000,000} \times 100 \% = 10.66 \% \).

The annual return on Marina's transactions is \( \frac{10.66 \%}{3} = 3.55 \% \).
A 10,000-meter race involves three participants: A, B, and C. A starts last. During the race, A exchanges positions with B and C a total of 9 times. Determine the final position of A in the race.

Armen paid \$190 to buy movie tickets for a group of \( t \) people, consisting of some adults and some children. Movie tickets cost \$5 for children and \$9 for adults. How many children's tickets did he buy?

Two people play a math game. Player A selects a group of single-digit integers \( x_{1}, x_{2}, \cdots, x_{n} \) as the secret numbers, which can be positive or negative. Player B can ask questions about the sum \( a_{1} x_{1} + a_{2} x_{2} + \cdots + a_{n} x_{n} \), where \( a_{1}, a_{2}, \cdots, a_{n} \) can be any set of numbers. Determine the minimum number of questions Player B needs to ask in order to guess the secret numbers.
The medians of one triangle are equal to the sides of another triangle. Find the ratio of the areas of these triangles.
Giuseppe has a sheet of plywood that measures $22 \times 15$. Giuseppe wants to cut out as many rectangular pieces of $3 \times 5$ as possible from it. How can he do this?

Marco visits Ristorante Machiavelli every Thursday for dinner. He has been a regular customer for 5 years. Each visit, he orders his favorite pasta dish for $12 and a dessert for $5. Every third visit, he also orders a special appetizer for an additional $8. How much money has Marco spent on average at the restaurant each year, considering he visits every week without missing a Thursday?

Alex is a barista who works at a coffee shop and dreams of becoming a lawyer. Every week, Alex works 25 hours at the coffee shop and earns $12 per hour. Alex has been saving money to pay for law school, which costs $15,000 per year. Alex also seeks advice from a successful lawyer, who recommends setting aside an additional $500 each year for books and other materials.

If Alex plans to save enough money to cover one year of law school tuition and the additional cost for books and materials in 3 years, how many hours must Alex work each year to meet this goal, assuming all earnings are saved for this purpose?

A group of sports bloggers are analyzing the performance of a basketball team over a recent series of games. They have collected statistics for 5 different games. In each game, the team scored the following points: 98, 105, 87, 112, and 95. To provide a more meaningful analysis, the bloggers want to find the average points scored per game. Additionally, they notice that the team's star player was responsible for scoring 30% of the total points across all games. How many points did the star player score in total during these 5 games?

Dr. Alex, a computer scientist, is exploring the technical feasibility of teleportation devices described in a popular sci-fi author's books. In the novel, each teleportation device requires 5 energy crystals to function, and each crystal can only power the device for 3 hours. 

Dr. Alex plans to test the devices for a full day (24 hours) to analyze their feasibility. If she has a supply of 50 energy crystals, how many devices can she test for the entire 24-hour period without running out of crystals?

A young researcher is analyzing the impact of social media on populist rhetoric. She decides to study the number of times certain keywords appear in social media posts over a week. On Monday, she finds 15 posts containing the keywords. On Tuesday, she finds 12 more posts than on Monday. On Wednesday, she collects data and finds half the number of posts she found on Tuesday. On Thursday, she discovers twice as many posts as she found on Monday. Finally, on Friday, she encounters 5 fewer posts than on Thursday. How many posts did she find in total from Monday to Friday?

Jamie owns a small bakery and is looking for an efficient and flexible financial service platform to manage her transactions. In one week, Jamie made 45 sales, with each sale averaging $12. She found a platform that charges a fixed monthly fee of $30 and an additional fee of $0.50 per transaction. If Jamie decides to use this platform, how much would she pay in fees for that week?

A songwriter is trying to write a new song with unique and compelling lyrics. They decide that each verse of the song should have 8 lines. The songwriter plans to write 5 verses for the song. If they have a total of 120 unique words they can use, how many times will each word be used, on average, throughout the entire song?

Jean Boucher is a history enthusiast who loves exploring her family's past. She recently discovered that her ancestors, the Bouchers, had a tradition of collecting historical artifacts. In the 18th century, the Boucher family acquired 45 artifacts. Each generation, starting with the 19th century, added 15 more artifacts to the collection. Jean is the 5th generation since the 18th-century Bouchers. How many historical artifacts does Jean now have in her family collection?

Ahmed is a Pakistani Muslim community leader living in New York City, and he is organizing an interfaith dinner to promote global harmony. He invites people from different cultural backgrounds, including 12 from the Pakistani community, 15 from the local mosque, 18 from a nearby church, and 20 from a local synagogue. Each person brings a dish representative of their culture to share.

During the dinner, Ahmed notices that each dish is enough to serve 4 people. To ensure everyone can taste each dish, he wants to know how many servings will be required in total. Calculate the total number of servings required if each guest tries every dish.

Alex is a lifelong fan of Varien, also known as Nikki Kaelar, and loves to keep up with the artist's latest updates. Recently, Varien announced a series of 5 new music tracks. Each track is set to be released on a different day over the course of a week. As a dedicated fan, Alex plans to listen to each new track 3 times on the day it's released, and an additional 2 times each day for the rest of the week. 

How many total times will Alex listen to all of the new tracks by the end of the week?

The museum curator is designing a new exhibit about ancient writing systems. The exhibit will have 5 sections, each dedicated to a different ancient civilization's writing. The curator plans to display 12 artifacts in each section. In addition, the curator decides to add a special interactive display in each section that takes up the space of 2 artifacts. If the exhibit hall can only hold 50 artifacts in total, how many interactive displays can the curator add without exceeding the exhibit hall's capacity?

A movie producer specializing in CGI technology is working on a new film that features realistic animal characters. For one scene, the producer needs to create 8 different animals. Each animal requires 5 hours of CGI work to look realistic. Additionally, each animal character needs a 2-hour post-CGI review to ensure quality. If the producer can allocate 2 CGI artists working at the same time, how many total hours will it take for the CGI work and review of all the animals?

Dr. Smith, a cognitive psychologist, wants to conduct an experiment to explore how perception affects immersion in virtual reality. She plans to test different durations of VR sessions with a group of participants. Dr. Smith has chosen three different durations for the sessions: 15 minutes, 30 minutes, and 45 minutes. She decides to have 4 sessions of each duration, but 3 participants can only do the 15-minute sessions due to scheduling conflicts.

In total, how many VR session minutes will Dr. Smith conduct if she has 10 participants in the experiment and each participates in all the sessions they can attend?

Sarah owns a small business and is looking for affordable web design solutions. She receives three quotes from different web designers. The first quote is $500 for a basic website. The second quote is $650, which includes a basic website and additional support for 6 months at no extra cost. The third quote is $750, which includes a basic website, 6 months of support, and a special feature that normally costs $100. 

Sarah wants to decide based on the total cost for the first 6 months. If she chooses the first option, she will have to pay an additional $20 per month for support. Which option is the most affordable for Sarah if she wants support for 6 months?

Old Mr. Thompson, a retired gentleman with a penchant for storytelling, fondly recalls the days when he would enjoy a smoke while chatting with friends. Although those days are behind him, he always finds a way to see the silver lining in every situation. One sunny afternoon, while reminiscing about those times, he decides to count the number of good things that have come from quitting smoking.

He remembers that he used to smoke 20 cigarettes a day. After quitting, he saved $5 a day that he would have spent on cigarettes. He started saving this money exactly 3 years ago. In addition, he also gained 2 extra hours each day that he used to spend smoking, which he now uses for his favorite hobby: gardening.

The birth date of Albert Einstein is 14 March 1879. If we denote Monday by 1, Tuesday by 2, Wednesday by 3, Thursday by 4, Friday by 5, Saturday by 6, and Sunday by 7, which day of the week was Albert Einstein born? Give your answer as an integer from 1 to 7.

Suppose that \( n \) is a positive integer and that the set \( S \) contains exactly \( n \) distinct positive integers. If the mean of the elements of \( S \) is equal to \( \frac{2}{5} \) of the largest element of \( S \) and is also equal to \( \frac{7}{4} \) of the smallest element of \( S \), determine the minimum possible value of \( n \).

In a game called "set," all possible four-digit numbers consisting of the digits 1, 2, and 3 (each used exactly once) are considered. A triplet of numbers forms a set if for each digit position, either all three numbers have the same digit, or all three numbers have different digits.

For example, the numbers 1232, 2213, 3221 form a set because in the first position, all three digits (1, 2, and 3) are present; in the second position, only the digit 2 is present; in the third position, all three digits are present; and in the fourth position, all three digits are present. The numbers 1123, 2231, and 3311 do not form a set because in the last position there are two 1s and a 3.

How many total sets exist in the game?

(Note: Rearranging the numbers does not create a new set. For instance, 1232, 2213, and 3221 is considered the same set as 2213, 1232, and 3221.)

Determine all triples \((p, q, n)\) that simultaneously satisfy
$$
\begin{array}{l}
q^{n+2} \equiv 3^{n+2}\left(\bmod p^{n}\right), \\
p^{n+2} \equiv 3^{n+2}\left(\bmod q^{n}\right)
\end{array}
$$
where \( p \) and \( q \) are odd prime numbers, and \( n \) is an integer greater than 1.

In the state of Karnataka, there are 224 assembly constituencies. During the last election, Party A won 56 seats, Party B won 78 seats, and Party C won 62 seats. The remaining seats were won by independent candidates. If the total number of votes cast in the election was 10,000,000 and each constituency had an equal number of votes, how many votes, on average, did independent candidates receive per constituency they won?

Mr. Johnson, a retired bank security officer, often reminisces about his days of protecting the bank from criminals. One day, he decides to organize his old case files. He has 28 files, each representing a crime he helped prevent. He wants to divide these files into 4 equal stacks so he can easily review them one at a time each week. Additionally, he discovers 3 extra files that were misplaced, and decides to add them evenly to the stacks. How many files will each stack contain after he adds the extra files?

Sara, a homesteader living off the grid, has a sustainable farm where she grows vegetables and raises chickens. She collects eggs from her chickens every morning. This week, Sara collected the following number of eggs each day: Monday - 12, Tuesday - 15, Wednesday - 10, Thursday - 13, Friday - 11. On Saturday and Sunday, she collects twice the average number of eggs she collects on weekdays. How many eggs does Sara collect in total during the week?

Alex is a train travel aficionado who is planning a railway circumnavigation trip around the world. He plans to visit 5 continents, spending an equal number of days on each continent. The total duration of his trip is 60 days. During his travels, Alex will use 10 different trains, with each train journey taking an average of 4 hours. If he travels every second day, how many hours in total will Alex spend on trains during his circumnavigation journey?

The master magician, known for their secretive nature, has 5 different magic tricks that they perform at special shows. Each trick requires a unique set of magic cards, and the magician has a total of 60 magic cards in their collection. To prevent anyone from learning their secrets, the magician ensures that no two tricks share more than 2 cards in common.

If each magic trick uses the same number of magic cards, how many cards does each trick use?

A structural engineer is designing a minimalist penthouse that incorporates a series of identical triangular glass panels as part of the rooftop design. Each triangular panel has a base of 3 meters and a height of 4 meters. The engineer needs to install a total of 10 panels to complement the modern aesthetic while ensuring structural integrity.

To secure each panel, the engineer uses 5 bolts per meter along the perimeter of the triangle. Calculate the total number of bolts needed to install all 10 panels. 

Remember that the perimeter of a triangle is the sum of the lengths of all its sides. The sides of each triangle are calculated using the base and the two equal legs formed by the height and half of the base.

Alex is a perfectionist when it comes to coding, and he spends a lot of time ensuring every detail is correct. One night, Alex is debugging a piece of code and notices that for every misplaced variable he finds, it takes him 15 minutes to fix it. In the first hour, he finds 3 misplaced variables. In the second hour, he becomes more efficient and finds 5 misplaced variables. By the third hour, he has found and fixed all the misplaced variables.

If Alex spent a total of 2.5 hours debugging, how many misplaced variables did he fix in total during these 2.5 hours?

At the veterans' hospital, the aged but lively administrator is organizing a special event for 120 veterans. She is known for her efficiency and excellent organizational skills, so she has decided to arrange the veterans into groups for different activities. Each activity requires a specific number of participants: painting needs 12 veterans, gardening needs 15 veterans, and storytelling needs 18 veterans. The administrator wants to ensure that all veterans participate in at least one activity. How many veterans will be left without an assigned activity if she assigns the maximum possible number to each of these three activities?

Abby has 7 pieces of candy and Ben has 15. They decide to give some candy to their little brother Carl, with Ben giving 2 more pieces than Abby. Compute the number of positive divisors of the total number of ways they can give candy to Carl.

The roots of \(f(x)=x^8+x^7-x^5-x^4-x^3+x+1\) are all roots of unity. A real number \(r\in[0,1)\) is called nice if \(e^{2\pi i r}\) is a root of \(f(x)\) and has positive imaginary part. Let \(S\) be the sum of all nice \(r\). If \(S=\frac{p}{q}\) in lowest terms, find \(p+q\).

Let \(S_5\) be the set of permutations of \(\{1,2,3,4,5\}\), and let \(C\) be the convex hull of the set \(\{(\sigma(1),\sigma(2),\dots,\sigma(5)) : \sigma \in S_5\}\). Determine the total number of 2-dimensional faces of the polyhedron \(C\).
In a certain year, a specific date was never a Sunday in any month. Determine this date.

find the faces of the <u>massivest</u> polyhedral that it's image on every three plane  $xy$ , $yz$  and  $zx$  is a good  $12$ -gon.
